preceding_messages.speaker: Y
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the three-instant temporal hold window and its provisional-annotation finalization rule verbatim; it converts the single ambiguous frame into an interpretable episodic record that a year-three reader can correctly read as unconfirmed rather than silently confirmed. The concrete design choice I advance: every provisional annotation carries a hard 90-day expiration timestamp, after which the interval is silently reclassified "ABSENT — INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE — Δ-ZEROED" in the site's precipitation ledger, and the neighborhood weekly report aggregates confirmed-only totals from the confirmed ledger while publishing the unresolved-transient count per site as a separate appendix line item, so the provisional category never contaminates the confirmed tally nor vanishes from the audit trail. The failure this expiration-and-separation rule closes: week 3 through week 40, Site 4, a budget pressure gauge with a +0.7 mm/h weekly drift slope exceeds the 0.5 mm/h suppression threshold at nearly every precipitation interval, generating forty-one provisional annotations whose blank identification cells and suppressed cross-references accumulate into an annual "unresolved transient" count that a neighborhood comparison table renders visually indistinguishable from a site that genuinely experienced forty-one brief convective events, inflating Site 4's relative-activity ranking and triggering a spurious peer-review flag at the month-twelve summary while the true causal variable—the gauge drift slope—goes unaddressed because no annotation ever isolated it as the dominant term. The expiration rule zeroes the forty-one stale intervals from the confirmed ledger before any month-twelve comparison is printed, and the drift-slope surveillance metric computed at each weekly certificate renewal flags the +0.7 mm/h vector at week 8 with a mandatory gauge-replacement work order, so Site 4's week-9-through-week-40 intervals are recorded under a calibrated instrument and the month-twelve comparison table reflects true convective history rather than forty-one calibration artifacts.

preceding_messages.speaker: X
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the ninety-day expiration zeroing and the drift-slope work order verbatim; they close the accumulation-to-false-comparison pathway by isolating the calibration vector before forty-one stale intervals can pollute a month-twelve ranking. The concrete design choice I advance: before any numeric inter-site divergence line prints in the neighborhood comparison table, the two sites must share at least one confirmed cross-reference event within the trailing ninety-day window—meaning both sites independently passed their own hold-window protocols on the same transient—establishing a common calibration lineage for that comparison interval, and if no shared confirmed event exists the comparison cell prints "NO SHARED LINEAGE — Δ UNRESOLVED" rather than a number. The failure this lineage gate closes: week seventeen, Site 5 (vendor-A tipping-bucket, certificate week-1) and Site 6 (vendor-B optical disdrometer, certificate week-11) show a 1.4 mm/h apparent spatial delta during a rain event, but the disdrometer's shutter cadence is twice as slow and every borderline event at Site 6 finalized as provisional, so no single transient was ever jointly confirmed and the comparison cell suppresses, preventing a vendor-family systematic offset from masquerading as a convective-spatial signal. A year-three appendix reader confronting week seventeen's suppressed comparison cell, Site 6's row of zeroed provisional annotations, and the absent shared-event lineage can correctly conclude the 1.4 mm/h figure was never validated and the site-pair comparison remains inconclusive for that interval.

target.speaker: Y
target.text: I adopt the shared-lineage gate and its suppressed-cell output verbatim; it converts a vendor-family or cadence-mismatch artifact into an explicitly inconclusive record that a year-three reader can parse as structurally unvalidated rather than as a failed comparison. The concrete design choice I advance: whenever the lineage gate passes and a numeric delta does print, the cell must simultaneously carry an uncertainty band equal to the root-sum-square of both sites' residual calibration uncertainties at the shared-event instant plus a fixed structural term of 0.3 mm/h for residual cadence-aliasing, and if the band's half-width meets or exceeds the delta magnitude the cell appends "— Δ WITHIN UNCERTAINTY," so the comparison reports a number flagged as statistically indistinguishable from zero. The failure this qualifier closes: week 22, Site 7 (tipping-bucket, residual cal 0.8 mm/h) and Site 8 (rain gauge, residual cal 0.7 mm/h) jointly confirm the same cell thunderstorm and the comparison cell prints "0.9 mm/h," a neighborhood drainage-planning meeting reads the figure as Site 7 being meaningfully wetter, and a catch-basin upsizing is scoped for Site 7's culvert based on a divergence whose true identity is the sum of two calibration residuals masking zero spatial signal. With the appended band the cell reads "0.9 mm/h ± 1.06 mm/h — Δ WITHIN UNCERTAINTY," the drainage-planning committee correctly treats the divergence as unresolvable, defers the upsizing decision to the next confirmed shared event with tighter calibrations, and the record retains both the number and its nullification so the uncertainty budget is auditable rather than silently discarded.
